If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to compensate for downward bias.

If sentiment swings from positive to negative over 3–5 days, shift forecast downward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >1.5% from recent 7-day average, apply a 0.5–1.0% correction toward the average in late horizon (16–30 days).

If sentiment is positive but recent price action shows strong downward momentum, reduce forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon to align with sentiment-driven volatility.

If sentiment is negative but recent price action shows strong upward momentum, increase forecast by 1–2% in mid-horizon to counteract sentiment-driven volatility.
